value.hook: Before changing event-rearmed retry budgets or registration error classification; see #281.
value.title: Retry budgets follow rearming events, not seat lifetimes

sections.name: body
sections.value:
Complements “Busy reads need safety and retry eligibility”; #281 closes that note's F232 follow-up.

Test budget rearming immediately after exhaustion, without an intervening quiet tick: quiet ticks can clear the old counter and hide a missing reset. Also fail a read inside registration, not only the preliminary pane probe. Runtime/Retryable errors decided nothing; stable refusals remain Seen. The exhaustive RegistrationError::is_transient match now expresses this distinction. NativeHolderCurrent/NativeSessionHold cannot arise from CodexBinder's Ordinary registration path, so their classification does not change plan 168's native-holder brake.

Name the budget's scope honestly. Any new global thread lock refreshes every pending row's three-retry budget; unrelated ongoing starts mean no seat-lifetime cap. The existing global trigger already probed every row on each start. For N failing rows, observed-start rate lambda and interval I (default 5 s), additional quiet retries are at most 3*N*lambda probes/s; total remains at most N/I. Registration retries pay the full existing attempt, not merely mocked Facts stages.

Both original stall repros passed on b803bdb, alongside all 12 committed tests and a frequent-start probe (15/15). Final PASS: reviewer output 20-verdict-pr-281-b803bdb.dd.json, commit 7c4dda4e. FakeRegistry::script_put_error is the reusable write-failure seam.
